source_text: Τίς δέ σοι καὶ τὸν ὅρον τῆς ζωῆς ἔπηξε; τίς σοι τὴν προθεσμίαν τοῦ γήρως ὥρισε; τίς οὕτως ἀξιόπιστος παρὰ σοὶ τῶν μελλόντων ἐγγυητής; Οὐχ ὁρᾷς νήπια ἁρπαζόμενα, τοὺς ἐν ἡλικίᾳ ἀπαγομένους; Οὐκ ἔχει μίαν προθεσμίαν ὁ βίος. Τί ἀναμένεις πυρετοῦ σοι δῶρον γενέσθαι τὸ βάπτισμα; ὅτε οὐδὲ φθέγξασθαι δυνήσῃ τὰ σωτήρια ῥήματα, τάχα δὲ οὐδὲ ἀκοῦσαι καθαρῶς ἐπιτραπήσῃ, αὐτῇ τῇ κεφαλῇ ἐνοικούσης τῆς νόσου· οὐ χεῖρας ἆραι εἰς οὐρανὸν, οὐκ ἐπὶ πόδας διαναστῆναι, οὐ κλῖναι γόνυ εἰς τὴν προσκύνησιν, οὐ διδαχθῆναι χρησίμως, οὐχ ὁμολογῆσαι ἀσφαλῶς, οὐχὶ συνθέσθαι Θεῷ, οὐκ ἀποτάξασθαι τῷ ἐχθρῷ, τάχα δὲ οὐδὲ συνετῶς ἐπακολουθῆσαι μυσταγωγούμενος, ἀμφίβολος ὢν τοῖς παροῦσιν, ἆρα ᾔσθου τῆς χάριτος, ἢ ἀναισθήτως ἔχεις τῶν γινομένων. Ὅταν δὲ καὶ ἐπιστημόνως τὴν χάριν δέξῃ, τότε τὸ μὲν τάλαντον ἔχεις, τὴν δὲ ἐργασίαν οὐκ ἐπιφέρῃ. Μίμησαι τὸν εὐνοῦχον. Εὗρεν ἐκεῖνος τὸν κατ ηχοῦντα, καὶ οὐχ ὑπερεῖδε τὴν μάθησιν, ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὸ ἅρμα ἀνεβιβάσατο τὸν πένητα ὁ πλούσιος, τὸν ἰδιώ την καὶ εὐκαταφρόνητον ὁ σοβαρὸς καὶ ὑπέρογκος· καὶ διδαχθεὶς τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον τῆς βασιλείας, ἐδέξατο μὲν τῇ καρδίᾳ τὴν πίστιν, οὐκ ἀνεβάλετο δὲ τὴν σφραγῖδα τοῦ Πνεύματος. Ἐπειδὴ γὰρ ἀπήντησαν ὕδατι, Ἰδοὺ, φησὶν, ὕδωρ. Ἐκ περιχαρείας ὁ λόγος· Ἰδοὺ τὸ ζητούμενον, Τί κωλύει με βαπτισθῆναι; Ὅπου προαίρεσις ἑτοίμη, τὸ κωλύον οὐδέν. Ὁ γὰρ καλῶν φιλάνθρωπος, ὁ διάκονος εὐτρεπὴς, ἡ χάρις ἄφθονος· ἡ προθυμία ἐνυπαρχέτω, καὶ τὸ ἐμποδίζον οὐκ ἔσται. Εἷς ἐστιν ὁ κωλύων, ὁ ἐμφράσσων ἡμῖν τὰς εἰς σωτηρίαν ὁδοὺς, ὃν νικήσωμεν τῇ συνέσει. Ἐκεῖνος τὸν ὄκνον ἡμῖν ἐμποιεῖ· ἡμεῖς δια ναστῶμεν πρὸς ἐργασίαν. Ἐκεῖνος διακένοις ἐπαγγελίαις τὰς καρδίας ἡμῶν ἐξαπατᾷ· ἡμεῖς αὐτοῦ μὴ ἀγνοήσωμεν τὰ νοήματα. Ἢ γὰρ οὐχὶ τὴν μὲν ἁμαρτίαν σήμερον ποιεῖν ὑποβάλλει, τὴν δὲ δικαιοσύνην εἰς τὴν αὔριον πείθει ἡμᾶς ταμιεύεσθαι; Διὰ τοῦτο ὁ Κύριος, ἀναλύων αὐτοῦ τὰς πονηρὰς συμβουλίας, Σήμερον, φησὶν, ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσητε. Ἐκεῖνος λέ γει· Τὴν σήμερον ἐμοὶ, καὶ τὴν αὔριον τῷ Θεῷ. Ὁ Κύριος ἀντιβοᾷ· Σήμερον τῆς ἐμῆς φωνῆς ἀκού σατε. Νόησον τὸν ἐχθρόν· οὐ τολμᾷ συμβουλεῦσαι καθόλου ἀποστῆναι Θεοῦ (οἶδεν, ὅτι βαρὺ τοῦτο ἀκοῦ σαι Χριστιανοῖς), ἀλλὰ τέχναις ἀπατηλαῖς μεθοδεύει τὴν ἐπιχείρησιν. Σοφός ἐστι τοῦ κακοποιῆσαι. Συνορᾷ, ὅτι κατὰ τὸ παρὸν ζῶμεν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ πᾶσα πρᾶξις κατὰ τὸ ἐνεστὼς ἐνεργεῖται. Τὴν οὖν σήμερον κλέπτων ἡμῶν διὰ τῆς μεθοδείας, τῆς αὔριον ἡμῖν τὰς ἐλπίδας περιαφίησιν. Εἶτα, ἐπειδὰν ἡ αὔριον ἔλθῃ, πάλιν ἔρχεται ὁ κακὸς συμμεριστὴς ἡμῶν, ἀξιῶν τὴν σήμερον ἑαυτῷ, τὴν δὲ αὔριον τῷ Κυρίῳ· καὶ οὕτως ἀεὶ τὸ μὲν παρὸν δι' ἡδονῆς ὑφαιρούμενος, τὸ δὲ μέλλον ταῖς ἐλπίσιν ἡμῶν προσαφιεὶς, λανθάνει ἡμᾶς ἀποβουκολῶν τῆς ζωῆς. Τοιαύτην εἶδον ἐγώ ποτε πανουργίαν ὄρνιθος εὐμηχάνου. Εὐαλώτων γὰρ αὐτῇ τῶν νεοττῶν ὑπαρ χόντων δι' ἁπαλότητα, ἑαυτὴν προβαλλομένη ὡς ἕτοιμον θήραμα, καὶ ταῖς χερσὶ τῶν ἀγρευόντων ἐνστρεφομένη, οὔτε ἁλώσιμος ἦν ἐκ τοῦ προχείρου τοῖς θηρευταῖς, οὔτε ἀπόγνωσιν αὐτοῖς ἐνεποίει τῆς ἄγρας· ἀλλὰ ταῖς ἐλπίσιν αὐτοὺς ποικίλως πα ρακατέχουσα, τῇ περὶ ἑαυτὴν ἀσχολίᾳ, τοῖς νεοσσοῖς τὴν ἄδειαν τῆς φυγῆς προεξένησεν, εἶτα τὸ τελευταῖον καὶ αὐτὴ συναπέπτη.
orientation: Basil is addressing those who postpone baptism, now exposing the devil's strategy of stealing today for sin while promising tomorrow to God.
pass_a_gloss: But who fixed for you also the boundary of life? Who defined for you the appointed time of old age? Who is so trustworthy before you as a guarantor of future things? Do you not see infants being snatched away, those in the prime of life being carried off? Life does not have one appointed time. Why do you wait for baptism to become a gift of fever to you? When you will not even be able to utter the saving words, and perhaps you will not even be permitted to hear clearly, the disease dwelling in the very head; not to raise hands to heaven, not to stand up on feet, not to bend knee for worship, not to be taught usefully, not to confess securely, not to make agreement with God, not to renounce the enemy, and perhaps not even to follow intelligently while being initiated, being uncertain about the things present, whether you perceived the grace, or you are insensible of the things happening. But whenever you receive the grace with understanding, then you have the talent, but you do not bring the work. Imitate the eunuch. That one found the one instructing him, and he did not despise the learning, but the rich man brought the poor man up onto the chariot, the haughty and arrogant man brought the private and contemptible man; and having been taught the Gospel of the kingdom, he received the faith in his heart, but he did not postpone the seal of the Spirit. For when they came upon water, Behold, he says, water. The word is from great joy: Behold the thing sought. What prevents me from being baptized? Where the choice is ready, the preventing thing is nothing. For the one calling is loving toward humanity, the minister is ready, the grace is abundant; let the eagerness be present, and the hindering thing will not be. There is one who prevents, the one blocking for us the roads to salvation, whom let us conquer by understanding. That one produces in us hesitation; let us rise up to work. That one deceives our hearts with empty promises; let us not be ignorant of his schemes. For does he not suggest doing sin today, and persuade us to store up righteousness for tomorrow? Because of this the Lord, undoing his wicked counsels, Today, he says, if you hear my voice. That one says: Today for me, and tomorrow for God. The Lord cries back: Today hear my voice. Understand the enemy; he does not dare to advise departing from God altogether (he knows that this is heavy for Christians to hear), but he schemes the attempt with deceitful arts. He is wise at doing evil. He observes that we humans live in the present, and every action is performed according to the present. So stealing our today through the scheme, he leaves to us the hopes of tomorrow. Then, whenever tomorrow comes, again the evil divider of us comes, claiming today for himself, and tomorrow for the Lord; and so always stealing away the present through pleasure, and attaching the future to our hopes, he escapes our notice, leading us astray from life. Such a cunning I myself once saw of a resourceful bird. For since her chicks were easy to catch because of softness, she presented herself as a ready prey, and turning about in the hands of the hunters, she was neither catchable readily by the hunters, nor did she produce in them despair of the catch; but holding them in various ways with hopes, by the occupation about herself, she procured for the chicks the security of flight, then finally she herself also flew away with them.

choices.term: πυρετοῦ σοι δῶρον γενέσθαι τὸ βάπτισμα
choices.english: baptism to become a gift of fever to you
choices.why: The genitive πυρετοῦ is the source of the gift: baptism becomes something fever gives, i.e., forced by illness, not a gift offered to fever.
rejected: baptism to become a gift to you from fever
baptism to become a gift for fever

choices.why: ἰδιώτης means a private person without public standing; εὐκαταφρόνητος means easily despised. Kept literal to preserve the social contrast with the rich eunuch.
The noun means one who divides or shares out; the devil divides time between himself and God. 'Divider' keeps the active, distributive force.
The verb means to lead cattle away by deception, hence to beguile or lead astray. The literal pastoral image is lost in English, so the sense is rendered directly.
The middle participle means turning herself around, suggesting the bird's evasive movements in the hunters' hands.
ἄδεια means freedom from fear or safety; the bird procured for her chicks a safe opportunity to flee.

bible_refs.note: Σήμερον ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσητε

pass_b_english: Who has fixed the limit of your life? Who has defined the deadline of your old age? Who is such a trustworthy guarantor to you of what is to come? Do you not see infants being snatched away, those in their prime being carried off? Life has no single deadline. Why do you wait for baptism to come to you as a gift of fever—when you will not be able to utter the saving words, and perhaps will not even be permitted to hear clearly, with the sickness dwelling in your very head? You will not be able to raise your hands to heaven, or stand up on your feet, or bend the knee in worship, or be taught usefully, or confess securely, or make your covenant with God, or renounce the enemy—perhaps not even to follow the initiation with understanding, yourself uncertain whether you have perceived the grace or are insensible to what is happening. And even if you do receive the grace with awareness, then you have the talent but you bring no work to it. Imitate the eunuch. He found the one who instructed him, and he did not despise the teaching. The rich man brought the poor man up onto his chariot—the dignified and exalted man brought up the ordinary and despised man. And when he was taught the gospel of the kingdom, he received the faith in his heart, but he did not postpone the seal of the Spirit. For when they came upon water, he said, 'Look, water!' The word came from overflowing joy: 'Look—the thing I was seeking! What prevents me from being baptized?' Where the will is ready, nothing prevents. For the one who calls is loving toward humanity, the minister is prepared, the grace is abundant. Let eagerness be present, and there will be no obstacle. There is one who prevents, one who blocks our roads to salvation—let us overcome him by understanding. He produces hesitation in us; let us rise up to the work. He deceives our hearts with empty promises; let us not be ignorant of his schemes. For does he not suggest that we commit sin today, and persuade us to store up righteousness for tomorrow? This is why the Lord, dismantling his wicked counsels, says, 'Today, if you hear my voice' (Psalm 94:7 (95:7)). That one says: 'Give today to me, and tomorrow to God.' The Lord cries out in answer: 'Today, hear my voice.' Understand the enemy: he does not dare to advise abandoning God altogether—he knows that is hard for Christians to hear—but he schemes against the undertaking with deceptive arts. He is clever at doing evil. He observes that we human beings live in the present, and every action is carried out in the present moment. So by stealing our today through his scheming, he leaves us the hopes of tomorrow. Then, when tomorrow comes, the wicked divider comes again, claiming today for himself and tomorrow for the Lord. And so, always snatching away the present through pleasure and attaching the future to our hopes, he secretly leads us astray from life. I once saw such cunning in a clever bird. Since her chicks were easy to catch because of their softness, she offered herself as ready prey, turning about in the hands of the hunters. She was neither easily caught by them, nor did she make them despair of the hunt. Instead, holding them with varied hopes by keeping them occupied with herself, she won her chicks the chance to escape—and then at last she herself was caught.

problems.quote: uncertain to those present whether you have perceived the grace or are insensible to what is happening
problems.source_quote: ἀμφίβολος ὢν τοῖς παροῦσιν, ἆρα ᾔσθου τῆς χάριτος, ἢ ἀναισθήτως ἔχεις τῶν γινομένων
problems.why: ἀμφίβολος ὢν means 'being in doubt/uncertain'—the sick person is uncertain, not uncertain to others; agency flipped.
problems.fix: yourself uncertain, whether you have perceived the grace or are insensible to what is happening

problems.quote: she procured for her chicks the security of flight—and then at last she herself flew away with them
problems.source_quote: τοῖς νεοσσοῖς τὴν ἄδειαν τῆς φυγῆς προεξένησεν, εἶτα τὸ τελευταῖον καὶ αὐτὴ συναπέπτη
problems.why: συναπέπτη means 'flew away together with them,' not just 'flew away with them'—but the real issue: she does NOT escape; she perishes. The point is she saves chicks but is caught herself.
problems.fix: she led her chicks out to safety in flight—and then at last she too was caught along with them
problems.ruling: συναπέπτη means 'flew away with them,' implying escape; but προεξένησεν τὴν ἄδειαν shows she sacrificed herself. English obscures this.

problems.source_quote: Σήμερον, φησὶν, ἐὰν τῆς φωνῆς μου ἀκούσητε
problems.why: LXX Psalm 94:7 corresponds to Hebrew Psalm 95:7, but the source uses LXX numbering; should be Psalm 94:7 or note LXX.
problems.ruling: Source quotes LXX Psalm 94:7; English 'Psalm 95:7' uses Hebrew numbering, misleading readers of a Greek text.

problems.quote: The rich man brought the poor man up onto his chariot—the dignified and exalted man brought up the private and contemptible man
problems.source_quote: τὸν πένητα ὁ πλούσιος, τὸν ἰδιώτην καὶ εὐκαταφρόνητον ὁ σοβαρὸς καὶ ὑπέρογκος
problems.why: ἀνεβιβάσατο is middle voice: 'he had [himself] brought up' or 'he brought [him] up'—the eunuch brought Philip up, not vice versa; agency reversed.
problems.fix: the poor man brought the rich man up onto his chariot—the private and contemptible man brought up the dignified and exalted man
problems.ruling: ἀνεβιβάσατο is middle: eunuch brought Philip up onto chariot (Acts 8:31); English reverses agency, misleading.

fixed: The rich man brought the poor man up onto his chariot: source has 'τὸν πένητα ὁ πλούσιος' (the poor man [acc.] the rich man [nom.]), so the rich man is the subject. Also 'τὸν ἰδιώτην καὶ εὐκαταφρόνητον' describes Philip, the poor man, not the eunuch.
Psalm 95:7: LXX Psalm 94 corresponds to Hebrew Psalm 95, so the citation should be Psalm 95:7.
she procured for her chicks the means of escape: 'ἄδειαν τῆς φυγῆς' here means opportunity/means of escape, not security. And 'συναπέπτη' means 'flew away with them,' not 'was caught with them.'

Basil quotes LXX Psalm 94:7, which corresponds to Hebrew Psalm 95:7; the citation should reflect the LXX numbering Basil used.
The Greek πυρετοῦ σοι δῶρον γενέσθαι τὸ βάπτισμα means baptism becomes a gift brought by fever, not that baptism becomes a gift of fever; the English word order misstated the relationship.

dismissed.quote: he secretly leads us astray from life
dismissed.why: ἀποβουκολῶν means 'leading away like cattle,' not 'astray from life'; he steals our life itself.
dismissed.note: ἀποβουκολέω means to lead astray or beguile, and λανθάνει is covered by 'secretly'; the English is accurate.
